entries.title: Ask in chat about a term or work
entries.body: On an article you added, each Glossary entry and each row in Citations has an Ask in chat button beside Dig deeper. It opens Chat with a question about that term or work already written, for you to edit; nothing is sent until you send it. Afterwards a mark on the entry reopens the most recent of those conversations beside the panel, and Chat's list shows which conversations began from a term or a cited work.

entries.title: Share an article while it is being added
entries.body: On the Add page, the sharing controls are in one Sharing section, closed until you open it, holding Make it public and a new Create a private link. Someone who opens a shared article before it has finished being added sees a Still being added page, which checks again every 10 seconds and has a Check now button. Before, they met the landing page or a Not shared message.

entries.title: Learn's addresses say learn, not remember
entries.body: Addresses for Learn now say learn rather than remember, as does Chat's Learn filter. An old bookmark still opens Learn, but one that named a view inside it opens on Recall, and an old link to the filter shows all conversations. Recall conversations keep their messages; a tab left open from before this version needs reloading.

entries.title: Bot-check pages are not saved as articles
entries.body: Some sites show a page checking you are not a bot before the article, and the app could save that page as the article. It now recognises one kind of these checks, and no others, and refuses it. It suggests saving the loaded page from your browser as PDF or HTML and uploading that.

entries.title: Failed Retry or Edit no longer hides messages
entries.body: In Chat, and in Learn's chat conversations, a Retry or Edit that failed before the answer began could leave a blanked answer or missing later messages until you reloaded. For a conversation already saved, the app now withdraws the attempt and shows what is saved. For a question that never sent, it keeps your question, including an edited version.

entries.title: Article title lines up with the text
entries.body: With the notes column beside the article switched on and no panel open, the title at the top of the page sat to the right of the text on tablet and small-laptop windows. It lines up with the text at every width.
